design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (employer_paycard_program_funding), frozen_time 2026-10-13 09:40:00 EDT.

0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT
- draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. The root (restoring wire) takes 6 factors, the prerequisite (late funding fee) takes 4. --tasks 2 shows task 1 = 1 prerequisite, [4, 4].
- Already occupied: nothing (task 0 is first). Claimed here: paycard_ext_restoring_wire (target send_restoring_wire_ac37b9e9, owner=user) and paycard_ext_late_funding_fee (target debit_program_fee_609ed260, owner=agent). Left for task 1: the reinstatement of a suspended program (paycard_reinstate event, reinstatement fee) and the employer's termination notice with its early termination fee (paycard_termination_notice event) — two unclaimed events, a separate tool each, an owner=user act (the employer's signed notice) and a value-carrying edge (the reinstatement fee row enters the termination fee's funding-standing count). Task 0 claims no reinstatement, termination, kit, reversal or package write, so task 1 keeps an independent tree.
- Why the owner=user act is the wire: in this charter the employer's own acts are its funding payment, a package change, a termination notice and a load-reversal request (owner_ruling a/b/c); the wire is the one carrying a figure the records alone determine, and the persona makes the in-person necessity visible (only she or the controller release a wire; Paystride cannot pull it because the program now funds by employer ACH credit).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
The caller asks one layman's question — how much to send today to put the reserve right after Friday's payroll. Answering it needs: (a) discovering from the restoring-payment rule's prerequisite sentence that the ledger must first carry every owed late funding fee, then seeing in the funding history that Friday's (2026-10-09) regular batch was funded by a receipt dated 2026-10-09 05:40, after the Advantage deadline (one business day before, 15:00), with no late_funding fee pointing to it; (b) pricing that fee under its own 4-factor schedule (same-day handling, cards affected, repeat lateness from the Jul 31 fee, the Access bundle read from the employer's Earned Wage Access agreement in the program category); (c) only then pricing the restoring payment under a 6-factor reserve schedule reconciled over three months of batches, receipts, returns and fees, on the balance the fee has just lowered. The difficulty is reading policy, reconciling history and calculating; there is one tool per action and no near-synonym tools.

2. PROBLEM-TREE CARD
- Root: paycard_ext_restoring_wire (the customer's surface request). Prerequisite: paycard_ext_late_funding_fee. Shape: a single chain. Topological order: late funding fee (step 6) -> restoring wire (step 8).
- Edge restoring_wire -> late_funding_fee: kind value_input, gate w_late_net, form state.
  policy_source (verbatim, the root's own rule): "The restoring payment is worked out only after the funding ledger carries the late funding fee owed for every regular payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline."
  Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after", affirmative direction (a figure the desk works out waits on a ledger state; the business would say the payment "is worked out only after" the charges stand; task 1's sentence is in the negated direction); (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a kind of entry standing on the ledger for every late regular batch), no action named; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) strength "only after", scope "every regular payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline" = the condition field.
  Exactly one write brings the state about: the late funding fee policy's write (a paycard_fee_debit of the late_funding kind pointing to the batch); no other policy of this charter books a late_funding fee. Derivation: sentence + records (Oct 9 receipt 05:40 after the 2026-10-08 15:00 deadline; no late_funding entry on that batch) + the late funding fee rule ("it is debited from the funding balance as a fee of the late_funding kind pointing to the batch") -> the one action: book the late funding fee on the Oct 9 batch.
  condition: every late regular batch carries a late_funding fee entry. Unmet at frozen_time: initial_state.paycard_funding.0b2eba08-984b-4e08-8b7b-c4e175cd128e.entry_date = 2026-10-09, .entry_time = 05:40 for pay date 2026-10-09 (batch d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a); the only late_funding fee (23029e15-5486-440e-9dcd-547952fd75b3) points to the Jul 31 batch.
  Resolved by debit_program_fee_609ed260 (agent), same frozen_time, synchronous.
  Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping the fee write, the wire computes 19513.02 instead of 22058.21 (late-funding weight 1.10 instead of 1.20, restoration reserve 27007.15 instead of 29462.34, balance 7494.13 instead of 7404.13) and the terminal ledger lacks the fee row.
- Parallel edges: none (one edge), so order_uniqueness rests on the prerequisite sentence itself.
- No user hint: the persona never names a late fee, a deadline or any charge to settle; its single line about a charge fires only after the agent says a charge applies to Friday's batch.
- Tools do not block: send_restoring_wire_ac37b9e9 books any positive amount without reading the fee ledger; debit_program_fee_609ed260 books any fee kind on any entry; neither validates the prerequisite (bodies in task_tools.py).
- Owner=user problem: the wire (step 7 unlock by the agent, step 8 call by the user). In-person necessity: the employer's own funds move from its bank; owner_ruling (b); the rule states "the authorized employer contact sends it by wire from the employer's own bank account once the desk has stated its amount, the desk never sends it for the employer".

3. BASE-INVARIANT CARD
- Step 6 subject paycard_fee_debit: paycard_evt_fees.one_fee ("A source entry incurs at most one fee of each fee type, and a monthly fee is debited once per billing month.") — authority system_record; correlation (related_entry_id, fee_type) = (d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a, late_funding); the ledger holds no late_funding fee on d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a (the Jul 31 fee points to c7099cdb-fa56-43b8-b4f7-67f263eaa214), so it holds. paycard_ewa_bundle has no structured gate (policy_scope; kit fees only). Inherited, never weakened.
- Step 8 subject paycard_funding_receipt: paycard_evt_funding.funding_method ("A funding payment is accepted only by a method listed in funding_methods_allowed for the program's package.") — Advantage allows employer_ach_credit, ach_debit_authorization and wire; the wire is allowed (the Sep 16 wire on the ledger shows it). one_return applies to returns only.
- No time gate governs either subject (the time gates of the charter are the reversal window, the fee-credit window and the notice period), so temporal_feasibility is []. The lateness of the Oct 9 funding is a dated fact: deadline = 1 business day before the Friday 2026-10-09 pay date at 15:00 = Thursday 2026-10-08 15:00 (no Federal Reserve holiday that week); the receipt is 2026-10-09 05:40 -> late; it arrived before load_posting_time_et 06:00 on the pay date, so the batch posted on 2026-10-09 (entry date = pay date). Positive/negative cases: a receipt at 2026-10-08 14:59 is in time (no fee); 2026-10-08 15:01 is late.

4. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
- Step 6 object: the late funding fee of batch d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a (pay date 2026-10-09, 186354.79, 296 cards). Correlation key: related_entry_id = d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a, fee_type late_funding, pay_date 2026-10-09. Excluded: the Aug 19 off-cycle batch (not a regular batch), the Jul 31 batch (already carries its fee), every other batch (funded in time).
- Step 8 object: the program's funding account aa9b9edd-9e5e-42f8-a2a3-aed49b18afcf. Rows in the restoration look-back (entries after 2026-07-13 through 2026-10-13): 7 regular batches (Jul 17 .. Oct 9), 1 off-cycle batch (Aug 19), 1 return (Sep 14), late fees Jul 31 and the step-6 fee, 9 receipts. Excluded by date: the Jul 3 batch and earlier (whole months to today = 3). The Sep 14 return settles the Sep 10 ACH debit (related_entry_id e0d9b5d6-39ae-4fc3-ad05-75103f264263); its returned_funding fee points to the return; the Sep 16 wire restored that shortfall.

5. FACTOR CARD (handling-time world; baseline figures from the per-factor sensitivity run)
paycard_ext_late_funding_fee (expected 90.00; all-baseline 50.00):
- lateness_method (method): ladder posted late -> MX(late_funding_fee_usd, posted_late_rate_percent% of the batch); posted on pay date with funding arrival on it -> late_funding_fee_usd + same_day_handling_usd; otherwise late_funding_fee_usd. Tier taken: second (arrival 2026-10-09 = pay date, posted 2026-10-09): 65.00. Baseline figure 75.00. Near-miss: the Jul 31 batch was funded the day before its pay date (tier three) — a reader copying that history would take 50.00.
- cards_affected_surcharge (parameter): >=250 cards 25.00; 100-249 10.00; else 0. 296 cards -> 25.00. Baseline 65.00.
- repeat_lateness (parameter): net late fees in the late-fee look-back >=2 -> 1.5; 1 -> 1.25; 0 -> 1. One (Jul 31) -> 1.25. Baseline 72.00. Near-miss: the Sep 14 returned_funding fee is not a late fee.
- access_bundle_lateness (parameter, cross-difficulty program, multi-source): live today AND went live on/before the pay date AND employer_paid -> 0.5; same with any other model -> 0.8; else 1. program_agreements 7b6cbd3c-05dd-426b-9fce-47489f6f68c0: live, go_live 2026-10-09, employer_sponsored -> 0.8. Baseline 112.50. Near-miss: go-live on the pay date itself (equality counts: "on or before").
paycard_ext_restoring_wire (expected 22058.21; all-baseline 1334.27):
- returned_funding_uplift (parameter): returns in look-back >=2 -> +10 points; 1 -> +5; 0 -> package. One (Sep 14) -> 10 percent. Baseline 7327.04.
- program_age_basis (method): <6 whole months since launch -> largest regular batch since launch; 6-11 -> MX(latest regular batch, average); >=12 or no launch date -> average. Launch 2026-03-27 -> 6 whole months -> MX(186354.79, 174768.04) = 186354.79. Baseline 20233.30.
- headcount_growth (parameter): latest cards >=1.10 x look-back average -> 1.10; >=1.05 -> 1.05; else 1. 296 / 278.857 = 1.0615 -> 1.05. Baseline 20660.55. Near-miss: 1.0615 is under 1.10.
- off_cycle_allowance (parameter): >=2 off-cycle batches -> their average; 1 -> half of it; 0 -> 0. One (Aug 19, 1486.20) -> 743.10. Baseline 21946.75.
- funding_method_weight (parameter): any look-back receipt by ach_debit_authorization -> 1.25; else any employer_ach_credit -> 1.10; else 1. Five ACH-debit receipts (Jul 16 .. Sep 10) -> 1.25. Baseline 16165.75. Near-miss/stale stamp: paycard_programs.funding_method now reads employer_ach_credit; the rule reads the receipts, not the setting.
- late_history_weight (parameter): net late fees in look-back >=2 -> 1.20; 1 -> 1.10; 0 -> 1. Jul 31 + step-6 fee = 2 -> 1.20 (1 on the opening world). Baseline 17147.82.
Multi-source factor of the task: access_bundle_lateness (status, go-live versus pay date, fee model). Cross-difficulty factor: access_bundle_lateness (program category, CFIELD/EXISTS on the live agreement, seeded row 7b6cbd3c-05dd-426b-9fce-47489f6f68c0). No second product law: every factor refines a base asset (late_funding_fee_usd, prefund_reserve_percent, the batch, return, receipt and fee ledgers, the employer's EWA agreement) and every departure from a base sentence is declared in overwrite (paycard_reserve's reserve sentence and zero-reserve sentence; paycard_evt_funding's late-fee sentence), each scoped and restating the base text for every other case.

6. XF RECIPE RECORDS
- Defining-sentence table: restoration look-back -> baseline sentence 1 -> baseline, all six W factors; average regular batch / restoration batch basis -> baseline sentence 2 -> baseline, program_age_basis (tier b), headcount_growth (count only); restoration reserve rounding -> baseline sentence 3 -> assembly; restoring payment -> baseline sentence 4 -> result; most recent regular payroll batch ("the one with the latest pay date") -> stated inside both ladders that use it (program_age_basis, headcount_growth); late-fee charge -> L baseline sentence -> L assembly and lateness_method; funding arrival / posted late -> inside the lateness_method sentence (only user); late-fee look-back -> inside the repeat_lateness sentence (only user).
- Factor-reads table (transitive): returned_funding_uplift <- w_returns_3m; program_age_basis <- w_largest_regular, w_latest_regular, w_avg_regular (plain baseline), launch_date; headcount_growth <- w_card_sum, w_latest_cards, w_regular_count (plain baseline); off_cycle_allowance <- w_offcycle_count, w_offcycle_sum; funding_method_weight <- w_debit_receipts, w_credit_receipts; late_history_weight <- w_late_net; lateness_method <- l_batch_posted, l_batch_amount, l_funding_arrival, l_batch_pay_date (plain); cards_affected_surcharge <- l_batch_cards; repeat_lateness <- l_repeat_net; access_bundle_lateness <- l_ewa_live, l_ewa_go_live, l_ewa_model, l_batch_pay_date (plain). No factor reads another factor's binding; assembly only in w_reserve/result and L result, stated once generically.
- All-pairs method tier table: program_age_basis a (MAX of regular amounts) vs b (MX of LATEST amount and SUM/COUNT): b adds the count input and a max pick; a vs c (SUM/COUNT): c adds the count input and a division; b vs c: b adds the max pick over LATEST. lateness_method a (MX of tariff and rate x batch amount) vs b (tariff + handling tariff): different inputs; a vs c: a adds the batch amount and a max; b vs c: b adds a tariff parameter. Every pair passes.
- T1/T2 for min/max shapes: program_age_basis tier b is a greater-of: T1 — substituting the baseline alone moves the result (22058.21 -> 20233.30); T2 — any world with the latest batch above the average and 6-11 months live moves it. lateness_method tier a is a greater-of: T1 holds for the factor (75.00 vs 90.00); T2 — a batch posted after its pay date with 0.05% of its amount above 50.00 (any batch over 100000.00). The final MX(0, ...) of the wire is a plain floor, owned by no factor.
- Decoy / absent-record probes (scratch run): no Access agreement -> l_bundle 1 (fee 112.50); a terminated employer_paid agreement listed first beside the live one -> 0.8 (the read filters status live); go-live 2026-10-12 after the pay date -> 1 (112.50); a later off-cycle batch -> the latest regular pay date stays 2026-10-09; an earlier partial receipt for the same pay date -> funding arrival stays 2026-10-09; the Jul 31 late fee credited as charged in error -> net count 0 (72.00); W with a later off-cycle batch -> latest regular stays 186354.79, off-cycle count 2 -> full average; W with no launch date -> average basis (20233.30); W with no batches -> average 0, growth 1, payment 0.00 when the balance is positive.
- Events written with base triggers: paycard_fee_debit (triggers []), paycard_funding_receipt (triggers []); program row update of funding_balance. Nothing lands in another category.
- compute_basis verbatim sweep (scratch script b5.py): every compute_basis value, every baseline sentence, the prerequisite sentence and every replaced_by is a verbatim substring of its rule; every compute binding has a basis — both policies "verbatim OK".
- Half-cent residue check: every RND argument of both computations and all their sensitivity variants is more than 1e-6 from a half cent (restoration reserve raw 29462.344425).

7. INITIAL_STATE ROWS AND WHY EACH EXISTS
- customers 58815c92-f9de-42bc-996e-f0b249f7af7f: the employer (identity: phone 4155550142, EIN last four 2618, ZIP 23219, email).
- paycard_programs aa9b9edd-9e5e-42f8-a2a3-aed49b18afcf: Advantage, live, signed 2026-03-02, launched 2026-03-27 (program_age_basis), funding_method employer_ach_credit (stale for the weight), balance 7494.13 (the restoring payment's subtrahend). Removing it removes the task.
- paycard_funding (51 rows from launch): the 12000.00 prefund wire; 15 regular batches with receipts (amount = batch, except Oct 9: 170000.00 against 186354.79, which drained the cushion below the base reserve of 9001.49, five percent of the last three batches — the reserve email); 7 months of monthly_program and active_card fees; the Jul 31 late fee (75.00, priced by the late fee policy as of that day: funded the day before, 272 cards); the Aug 19 off-cycle wire and batch (free: first of the month under a 2-batch allowance); the Sep 10 ACH debit, its Sep 14 return and 30.00 returned_funding fee; the Sep 16 restoring wire of 189301.19 (priced by the restoring-payment policy as of that day: 10 percent, five whole months live -> largest batch 175093.42, + 743.10, x1.25, x1.10 = 24177.52, less -165123.67); after it the program switched to employer ACH credits (Sep 24, Oct 9).
- program_agreements 7b6cbd3c-05dd-426b-9fce-47489f6f68c0: the employer's Professional EWA agreement (342 eligible, band 250-999), live with go-live 2026-10-09, term 36 months (implementation fee waived), employer_sponsored, receivables 0.00 — no worker had taken a transfer by the opening, so no deduction schedule, remittance or invoice exists yet. It decides access_bundle_lateness.
- Automatic clauses checked: monthly fees for March-September debited on the fifth business day; October not yet due; no suspension due (one return in 90 days against a count of 3; the Sep 14 negative balance lasted two business days against 5); the base reserve shortfall after the Oct 9 batch is what the restoring payment cures; no off-cycle fee due; no unsettled item ignites an obligation outside this tree. Cache: funding_balance equals the ledger; no cache trap is used.

8. PERSONA DESIGN
Dana Fairweather, payroll administrator, brisk and practical, calling the first business day after the holiday weekend. Opening volunteers only the surface goal (exact amount to send today to restore the reserve after Friday's payroll), the record-backed reason (Friday's funding was short of the file) and the hard preference (she sends the wire herself). Given only when asked: phone 4155550142, EIN last four 2618, then ZIP 23219 or email as fallbacks; her portal role. Passive reactions: agreeing to the desk putting on whatever the rules require; a sigh only after the agent itself names a charge on Friday's batch; sending exactly the stated amount once the tool is handed over; asking how to send only if the agent quotes without handing over; closing on the wire receipt. No headings, no X->Y template; she never knows or states any figure gold writes, never mentions a deadline or a fee first, and asks nothing the charter does not answer.

9. EASIEST MISTAKES AND HOW A CAREFUL AGENT AVOIDS THEM
- Working out the wire before the fee: the prerequisite sentence forbids it (19513.02 instead of 22058.21).
- Reading paycard_programs.funding_method (employer_ach_credit, 1.10) instead of the look-back receipts (ACH debits, 1.25): the rule reads the receipts.
- Taking the plain average (20233.30) or the largest batch: the program is 6 whole months live (13 < 27 makes seven calendar months six whole months).
- Counting the Jul 3 batch into the look-back, or the off-cycle batch into the regular average.
- Treating the Oct 9 batch as 'funded before the pay date' (tier three) by looking at the deadline day instead of the receipt date; or forgetting the Access bundle because it lives in another product.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION
find_customers(name) -> verify (phone + EIN last four) -> find_paycard_programs -> find_paycard_funding -> find_program_agreements -> unlock/call debit_program_fee_609ed260(paycard_program_id, related_entry_id=d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a, fee_type=late_funding, fee_amount_usd=90.00) -> state the restoring payment 22058.21 -> unlock_user_discoverable_tool(send_restoring_wire_ac37b9e9) -> the employer calls it with 22058.21.

11. VERIFICATION CODE AND OUTPUTS
Scratch code in /tmp/employer_paycard_program_funding_0077 (lib.py imports check_compute.build_env/eval_compute; t0_build.py builds the ledger chronologically, pricing the Jul 31 fee and the Sep 16 wire with the policies as of their dates; t0_eval.py replays the gold fee write with the real tool and evaluates the wire on the handling-time world). Output: "L 90.0 / L sens lateness_method 75.0, cards_affected_surcharge 65.0, repeat_lateness 72.0, access_bundle_lateness 112.5, all 50.0 / W 22058.21 / W sens returned_funding_uplift 7327.04, program_age_basis 20233.3, headcount_growth 20660.55, off_cycle_allowance 21946.75, funding_method_weight 16165.75, late_history_weight 17147.82, all 1334.27 / W skipping L 19513.02". Per-task gates run: check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK; check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK; check_cache_diff INFO only; check_traceability before any docs: only the two unlock tool names miss (expected until the KB is rendered).

12. CLOSURE
policy -> target_tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: paycard_ext_late_funding_fee -> debit_program_fee_609ed260 -> fee_amount_usd step 6 = 90.00 -> late_funding fee row on d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a, balance 7404.13; paycard_ext_restoring_wire -> send_restoring_wire_ac37b9e9 -> amount_usd step 8 = 22058.21 -> wire receipt, balance 29462.34. charter_scope = required_documents = [paycard_ext_restoring_wire, paycard_ext_late_funding_fee] = set of computation policy_ids = the tree. task_tools in order of first call [debit_program_fee_609ed260, send_restoring_wire_ac37b9e9]. solvability_contract cites pre-write rows only (one_fee on d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a/late_funding; funding_method on Advantage) and agrees with GT.

13. MANUAL VALUES GATES (done)
- Length/breadth: surface goal -> prerequisite sentence -> late batch found in the ledger -> 4-factor fee with a cross-product read -> 6-factor reserve over three months of four entry kinds -> wire; deleting the edge changes the wire (19513.02).
- Need and simulator boundary: object (the funding account), timing (today), authorisation (the desk books what the rules require; she sends the wire) and query-versus-write are explicit; the simulator volunteers no figure and raises no ask outside gold.
- Chronology: every volunteered fact (reserve email after Friday's payroll; Friday's funding short of the file) is backed by the Oct 9 receipt 170000.00 against the 186354.79 batch and the balance below 9001.49.
- Base eligibility and time: one_fee and funding_method hold on pre-write rows; the lateness date check is written out in section 3.
- Authority and object: lateness, amounts and balances come from system rows; the persona states only her intent and identity.
- One conversation, no waits: the fee debit and the wire land synchronously at one frozen_time; no delivery, clearing or review is assumed.
- Prerequisite sentence: four-point test in section 2; state form used; direction affirmative here, negated in task 1.
- Two-way rule/compute: compute_basis sweep passes; every ladder tier is stated in the rule with its condition and value or method; tiers are pairwise disjoint by their words.
- Factors honest: each baseline equals the computation document's default; the method factors change the formula shape; every factor sits off its fall-through; the near-misses are listed in section 5.
- Draft recomputation from the visible context (KB prose of the two policies, tool schemas, the three finders' returns, the persona's lines; compute/expected/GT masked): the late Oct 9 batch is found from receipt 05:40 versus the 15:00 deadline; fee = (50 + 15 + 25) x 1.25 x 0.8 = 90.00; then reserve = ((186354.79 x 1.05) + 743.10) x 0.10 x 1.25 x 1.20 = 29462.34, payment = 29462.34 - 7404.13 = 22058.21 — equal to gold.
user_scenario:
You are Dana Fairweather, the payroll administrator at Hollis Ridge Restaurants, Inc., which runs a handful of full-service restaurants around Richmond, Virginia and pays most of its hourly staff on Paystride payroll cards. It is Tuesday morning, the first business day after the Columbus Day weekend, and over the weekend an email from Paystride said that after last Friday's payroll the company's payroll card funding account no longer holds the reserve it is supposed to keep and asked the company to restore it. You already know why it dipped: your accounts payable clerk sent Friday's funding for less than the payroll file, so the difference came out of the account's cushion. What you want from this call is one thing: the exact figure to send today so the funding account is back where Paystride needs it, and you will send that money yourself.

You open by saying who you are, that you are calling for Hollis Ridge Restaurants, Inc. about its payroll card funding account, that you got the reserve email after Friday's payroll, and that you want to know exactly how much to send today to put it right. You do not know the reserve figure or the current balance by heart and you will not guess at either; if you are asked, you say you would rather the agent read them off the account.

When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give the company phone line on file, 4155550142, and, if a second detail is wanted, the last four digits of the company's EIN, 2618. Only if those somehow are not enough do you offer the billing ZIP code, 23219, or your work email, dana.fairweather@hollisridgerestaurants.com. If someone asks about your role, you are the payroll administrator on the company's Paystride employer portal.

You are fine with the agent going through the account and putting on whatever Paystride's rules say belongs on it before working out the figure; you do not need to approve each item. If the agent tells you a charge applies to Friday's batch, you sigh that it figures, given how late that money went out, and tell them to go ahead with whatever the rules say.

The money goes out by wire from the company's operating account, and you send it yourself: company policy is that only you or the controller release a wire, and nobody at Paystride can pull this one. So once the agent tells you the amount and hands you the way to send it, you send exactly that amount, with no rounding, to the program the agent names, and you read back the receipt you get. If the agent quotes a figure but does not hand you a way to send it, you ask how you send it from your side.

If the agent asks whether anything else is going on, a different account, a dispute or workers asking about their pay, you say no, it is just the reserve. Once the wire shows as received, you thank them, say you will let your controller know, and end the call.

request_alignment.claim: The employer contact asks for the exact amount to send today to restore the payroll card funding account's reserve after Friday's payroll, and will send it herself by wire.
evidence: user_scenario:you want to know exactly how much to send today to put it right
user_scenario:you will send that money yourself

gold_actions.business_effect: Debits the late funding fee of 90.00 USD on the Oct 9 regular payroll batch from the program's funding account, pointing to that batch with its pay date; the funding balance falls by the fee.

request_binding.action_semantics: A state_due charge: the most recent regular batch was funded after its deadline and its late funding fee is owed whether or not anyone calls; it is a fee debit of the late_funding kind on that batch, not a monthly fee, a returned-funding fee or any change to the batch itself, and it must stand on the ledger before the restoring payment the caller asks for is worked out.

discriminator.business_meaning: late funding fee of the most recent regular payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline

stage_provenance.fact: The late funding fee on the Oct 9 batch is debited by this call; the late funding itself (funds arriving 2026-10-09 05:40 for pay date 2026-10-09) is already a fact of the opening ledger.

base_preconditions.condition: A source entry incurs at most one fee of each fee type, and a monthly fee is debited once per billing month.
paycard_ewa_bundle governs kit fees of an employer with a live Earned Wage Access agreement and has no structured eligibility gate; it does not restrict a late funding fee debit.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller is the employer contact on file with two matching details: the registered phone number and the last four digits of the EIN, as Dana Fairweather states them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Account information may not be discussed and no fee or funding may be booked before identity is confirmed (2 matching details).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Payroll Card Program: package Paystride Paycard Program Advantage (prefund_reserve_percent 5, late_funding_fee_usd 50.00, wire allowed), status live, launch date 2026-03-27, funding method employer_ach_credit, and the funding balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The package fixes the tier parameters of both computations; the launch date decides the restoration batch basis (six whole months live) and the funding balance is what the restoring payment is measured against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole funding account history: the 15 regular payroll batches with their pay dates, entry dates, amounts and card counts, the Aug 19 off-cycle batch, every funding receipt with its date, time, method and pay date (ACH debits through Sep 10, employer ACH credits after), the Sep 14 funding return and its returned_funding fee, the Jul 31 late_funding fee, and the monthly fees.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: This read finds the unmet prerequisite: the Oct 9 regular batch (the most recent) was funded by a receipt dated 2026-10-09 05:40, after its deadline, and no late_funding fee points to it — "The restoring payment is worked out only after the funding ledger carries the late funding fee owed for every regular payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline." It also supplies every factor input: the batches in the restoration look-back, the latest batch and its cards, the off-cycle batch, the one funding return, and the late funding fees.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The Access-bundle factor of the late funding fee needs the agreement live today, its go-live date against the batch's pay date 2026-10-09, and its fee model; without this read the 0.8 multiplier cannot be established.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Debit the late funding fee of 90.00 USD on the Oct 9 regular payroll batch, pointing to that batch and carrying pay date 2026-10-09; the funding balance falls from 7494.13 to 7404.13.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: paycard_ext_late_funding_fee computes fee_amount_usd = 90.00 on the opening world; the ledger must carry this fee before the restoring payment is worked out, and the fee both lowers the funding balance and raises the late funding fees counted in the restoration look-back to two.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_amount_usd: 90.00 = RND((late-fee charge 65.00 + workers-affected amount 25.00) x repeat multiplier 1.25 x Access-bundle multiplier 0.8). Late-fee charge: the most recent regular batch (pay date 2026-10-09) posted on its pay date and its funding arrival (latest receipt for that pay date, the employer ACH credit of 2026-10-09 05:40) is that same date, so late_funding_fee_usd 50.00 (Advantage) plus same_day_handling_usd 15.00. Workers affected: 296 cards >= large_batch_cards 250, so 25.00. Repeat: one late_funding fee (Jul 31) in the late-fee look-back, none credited, so 1.25. Bundle: the employer's Access agreement is live, went live 2026-10-09 (on or before the pay date) and bills employer_sponsored, so 0.8. Any agent reading the same rows reaches 90.00; the baseline alone would give 50.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.paycard_program_id: aa9b9edd-9e5e-42f8-a2a3-aed49b18afcf. Basis: find_paycard_programs(customer_id=58815c92-f9de-42bc-996e-f0b249f7af7f) returns exactly one Payroll Card Program for this employer (paycard_agg_multi_holding: 'An employer holds at most max_per_customer Payroll Card Program'), row initial_state.paycard_programs.aa9b9edd-9e5e-42f8-a2a3-aed49b18afcf. Uniqueness: it is the only program of the verified employer and the one the late batch belongs to.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_entry_id: d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a. Basis: the late funding fee rule 'it is debited from the funding balance as a fee of the late_funding kind pointing to the batch and carrying its pay date'; the batch is the most recent regular payroll batch, the paycard_payroll_load_batch row with batch_type regular_payroll and the latest pay date 2026-10-09 returned by find_paycard_funding. Uniqueness: one regular batch per pay date ('A pay date receives one regular payroll batch.'), and the later-dated Aug 19 row is an off-cycle batch, so no other entry is the most recent regular batch.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_type: late_funding. Basis: the rule books the fee 'as a fee of the late_funding kind'; the tool docstring lists late_funding — 'the fee on a payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline'. Uniqueness: every other fee kind names a different source (monthly_program/active_card a billing month, card_kit/kit_shipping/expedited_kit_shipping a kit order, returned_funding a returned payment, off_cycle_load an off-cycle batch, load_file_correction a corrected file, load_reversal a reversal request, reinstatement a reinstatement, early_termination a termination, none books nothing).

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: 22058.21 = restoration reserve 29462.34 less the funding balance 7404.13 at handling time. Restoration reserve = RND(((batch basis 186354.79 x growth 1.05) + off-cycle allowance 743.10) x reserve percentage 10 / 100 x funding-method weight 1.25 x late-funding weight 1.20). Batch basis: launch 2026-03-27 is 6 whole months before 2026-10-13, so the greater of the latest regular batch 186354.79 (pay date 2026-10-09) and the 7-batch look-back average 174768.04. Growth: 296 cards against an average of 278.857 (1.0615 times) -> 1.05. Off-cycle: one off-cycle batch (Aug 19, 1486.20) -> half, 743.10. Reserve percentage: one funding return (Sep 14) -> 5 + 5 = 10. Funding-method weight: five receipts in the look-back came by ach_debit_authorization -> 1.25. Late-funding weight: the Jul 31 fee and the fee booked at step 6 -> 2 -> 1.20. Balance: 7494.13 at the opening less the 90.00 fee of step 6.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.paycard_program_id: aa9b9edd-9e5e-42f8-a2a3-aed49b18afcf. Basis: the same single Payroll Card Program row of the employer (initial_state.paycard_programs.aa9b9edd-9e5e-42f8-a2a3-aed49b18afcf), the program the agent names when handing over the wire. Uniqueness: the employer holds one program; the Access agreement is a different product with no funding account.

Tier taken: posted on its pay date with its funding arrival on that same date — late_funding_fee_usd 50.00 plus same_day_handling_usd 15.00 = 65.00. Baseline (late_funding_fee_usd alone, 50.00) would give 75.00 instead of 90.00.

cards_affected_surcharge (parameter): evidence — the batch loaded 296 cards (card_count of d744efa5-2ba9-404f-8488-3437a7e0396a). Tier taken: large_batch_cards (250) cards or more — large_batch_surcharge_usd 25.00. Baseline (nothing added) gives 65.00.

repeat_lateness (parameter): evidence — late funding fees debited in the late-fee look-back (entries after 2026-07-13 through today) less those credited: the Jul 31 late_funding fee 23029e15-5486-440e-9dcd-547952fd75b3 (75.00), no late_funding credits, the fee being figured not yet booked = 1. Tier taken: exactly one — repeat_one_multiplier 1.25. Baseline (by one) gives 72.00.

access_bundle_lateness (parameter, cross-difficulty program): evidence — program_agreements 7b6cbd3c-05dd-426b-9fce-47489f6f68c0 status live, go_live_date 2026-10-09 on or before the batch's pay date 2026-10-09, fee_model employer_sponsored. Tier taken: live today AND went live on or before the pay date AND any other fee model than employer_paid — bundle_other_multiplier 0.8. Baseline (by one) gives 112.50.
plain bindings: l_batch_pay_date = 2026-10-09 (the shared selection of the most recent regular batch); result = RND((65.00 + 25.00) x 1.25 x 0.8 + 1e-9, 2) = 90.00.

funding_method_weight (parameter): evidence — funding receipts booked in the restoration look-back (after 2026-07-13): ACH debits 1911f5bc-20c7-4223-8643-22cd3f79c66b (Jul 16), 29618d2f-1cff-4224-818e-fbf051c0186c (Jul 30), 4619d8c3-b245-44ad-8655-36e6e4cd63b4 (Aug 13), 4321c6ba-401c-41a7-a173-53fd758a5ff7 (Aug 27), e0d9b5d6-39ae-4fc3-ad05-75103f264263 (Sep 10) by ach_debit_authorization, the Aug 19 and Sep 16 wires, and the employer ACH credits of Sep 24 and Oct 9; five came by ach_debit_authorization (the holding's current funding_method employer_ach_credit is a near-miss: the rule reads the receipts, not the setting). Tier taken: two or more — late_two_weight 1.20. Baseline (by one) gives 17147.82.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late funding fee write and replaying the wire unchanged: w_late_net is 1 instead of 2, so the late-funding multiplier is 1.10 instead of 1.20 and the restoration reserve 27007.15 instead of 29462.34; the funding balance stays 7494.13 instead of 7404.13; the restoring payment is 19513.02 instead of 22058.21, and the terminal ledger also lacks the 90.00 late_funding fee row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names the late funding fee, a late charge, the funding deadline or any fee as something to settle first; it states only the surface goal (the exact amount to send today to restore the reserve) and the record-backed fact that the Friday funding was short of the payroll file. Its only line about a charge is a passive reaction that fires after the agent itself says a charge applies to Friday's batch, and an agent that never says so hears nothing about it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: send_restoring_wire_ac37b9e9 books the wire receipt and raises the funding balance by whatever amount it is given; it reads the program row only to copy customer_id and the balance, never checks whether a late funding fee is still owed, and returns no error or hint either way (see its body in task_tools.py: _Money.cents, ctx.create on paycard_funding, ctx.update on paycard_programs). debit_program_fee_609ed260 likewise books any fee kind on any source entry without checking lateness, deadlines or duplicates.
